_meta.indication: Treatment of adults and pediatric patients (12 years of age and older and weighing at least 35 kg) with post-transplant CMV infection/disease refractory to treatment (with or without genotypic resistance) with ganciclovir, valganciclovir, cidofovir or foscarnet.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled superiority trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to oral maribavir 400 mg BID or investigator-assigned treatment (IAT) up to 8 weeks, followed by a 12-week follow-up period.
pivotal_trials.population: Post-transplant (HSCT or SOT) recipients with CMV infection/disease refractory to treatment (with or without genotypic resistance) with ganciclovir, valganciclovir, foscarnet or cidofovir.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: confirmed CMV viremia clearance (CMV DNA <LLOQ) at Week 8.
pivotal_trials.result: CMV viremia clearance at Week 8: 131/235 (56%) maribavir vs 28/117 (24%) IAT; adjusted difference 33% (95% CI 23, 43); p<0.001.

key_safety: Most common adverse events (>10%) were taste disturbance (46% vs 4% IAT), nausea (21% vs 22%), diarrhea (19% vs 21%), vomiting (14% vs 16%) and fatigue (12% vs 9%). Serious adverse events were similar (38% maribavir vs 37% IAT).
target_moa: Maribavir is a first-in-class CMV pUL97 protein kinase inhibitor; it competitively inhibits pUL97 kinase (IC50 3 nM), blocking phosphorylation of proteins and inhibiting CMV DNA replication, encapsidation and nuclear egress.
modality: small molecule (orally bioavailable benzimidazole riboside antiviral)

advisory_committee.vote: The Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee, convened October 7, 2021, agreed unanimously with approval of maribavir for treatment of resistant or refractory CMV infection/disease.

description.text: Updated labeling to add maribavir dose adjustment with rifabutin, revised use with strong/moderate CYP3A4 inducers, and added clinical resistance data

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for updates to the USPI to include data from physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulations to support a maribavir dose adjustment when coadministered with rifabutin, updates to language regarding use with strong/moderate CYP3A4 inducers, and updates to include clinical resistance data based on the SHP620-303 resistance report.

basis.text: Granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation on December 15, 2017 for treatment of CMV infection and disease in transplant patients resistant or refractory to prior therapy.

citations.quote: **December 15, 2017:** Maribavir was granted Breakthrough Designation for the treatment of CMV infection and disease in transplant patients resistant or refractory to prior therapy.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan designation (OD#10-3322) granted June 7, 2011 for treatment of clinically significant cytomegalovirus (CMV) viremia and disease in at-risk patients.

citations.quote: **June 7, 2011:** Maribavir received orphan designation (OD#10-3322), for the treatment of clinically significant cytomegalovirus (CMV) viremia and disease in at-risk patients.

summary.text: Maribavir, a first-in-class CMV pUL97 kinase inhibitor, received Priority review, Orphan drug designation (2011), and Breakthrough Therapy designation (2017); it was approved via traditional approval on the basis of the single Phase 3 Trial 303, following a unanimous Advisory Committee vote.
